title: Replace a Broken Brass Harp String
summary: Lay harp down, remove old string, feed new brass wire through soundboard, tie toggle, trim, hook to tuning pin and wind to pitch.
warnings: Sharp brass wire ends can cut skin
Harp is heavy - lift carefully to avoid back injury or dropping
String under tension can snap during winding

steps.title: Lay harp on its back
steps.instruction: Lay the harp on its back on the ground to work on it.
warnings: Harp is heavy - lift carefully to avoid dropping or back injury

evidence.text: To replace a string, I'll work with work with the harp lying on its back on the ground.
Harp lying on its back on black cloth

steps.title: Remove old string
steps.instruction: Pull the old broken string off the harp and save it for reuse.
warnings: Sharp broken wire end can prick skin

evidence.text: The first thing I'm going to do is to pull the pull the old string off
I'm going to try and save this string because it's long enough to use use further up that octave so it can go into into my string bag.

steps.title: Turn harp onto right side
steps.instruction: Turn the harp down onto its right side to access pin, shoe and back.
warnings: Harp is heavy - support it while turning to prevent falling

evidence.text: Then I'll turn the harp down onto its right side.
and this will give me access to all the the things I need the pin at the top the shoe at the bottom and inside the back of the harp

steps.title: Feed new wire through harp
steps.instruction: Feed wire off the reel into the front hole and grab it through the back hole.
warnings: Sharp wire end can cut fingers - feed carefully

evidence.text: so I feed the wire into the harp off the reel I don't cut it to to length first
so you see how this works you just poke it into the front
and then grab it through the hole at the back.

steps.title: Tie toggle to wire
steps.instruction: Loop wire once around toggle and fold back in a hairpin to tie toggle knot.

evidence.text: and so here's the wire that's inside the harp I can tie the toggle to it because it's 0.6 that's thick enough to use a very simplest knots you just go round the toggle once and then you fold the wire back over itself in a hairpin

steps.title: Tighten knot and seat toggle
steps.instruction: Tighten toggle knot with pliers and pull wire through to seat toggle.
warnings: Pliers can pinch fingers - squeeze carefully

evidence.text: and then to make sure it's doesn't fall off when we're putting it in use the pliers to pull it nice and tight so there's my toggle knot and then all I do pull it through

steps.title: Cut wire and make hook
steps.instruction: Cut wire about five centimeters above pin and bend a small hook.
warnings: Cut wire ends are sharp - keep away from eyes and skin

evidence.text: I can cut it to length I don't know a few five centimeters above the pin
just snap it off with the pliers make a little hook and then I'll turn the harp up

steps.title: Turn harp upright
warnings: Harp is heavy - support it while turning

evidence.text: and then I'll turn the harp up
Hands lift and turn harp upright

steps.title: Hook string onto pin
steps.instruction: Hook the wire hook onto the tuning pin.

evidence.text: you can hook the hook onto the pin

steps.title: Wind and tune string
steps.instruction: Wind the string up with the tuning key and bring to pitch.
warnings: String under tension can snap - keep face clear and do not over-tighten

evidence.text: and then you can wind it up
